tw-mi-cambridge-jct-walker-tavern-money-.t: The chain runs from the 1922 'gold laden traveler murdered' to the 1941 WPA money belt and oak (repeated in a 1951 Detroit News Q&A, which has him found 'beneath the shattered window, in a crumpled heap on a flower bed'); no newspaper telling has a burial, and the 1879 and 1909 county histories mention no murder.
src: Detroit News, 1 Nov 1951, p. 37, readers' Q&A (Newspapers.com 1380789983)
Whitney & Bonner, History of Lenawee County (1879); Bonner, Memoirs of Lenawee County (1909); Portrait and Biographical Album of Lenawee County (1888): no murder
Saginaw News, 14 Jul 1940, p. 5 (Newspapers.com 1107609753): island 'in the middle of the upper bay', picnic and swimming spot

pinev: Placed from the source text: Frank G. Stocking letter 1914: "south side of the creek about 1/2 or 3/4 of a mile above the lake and about 10 rods back from the creek"; camp on E side of Little Wabasis Lake (GNIS 43.1539,-85.3594). Pin = creek midway between the lakes

1876 Kent atlas, Oakfield T9N R9W: the inlet creek runs S from Oakfield Centre past Little Wabasis (sec 22) and enters the lake's NE lobe in NW sec 27, matching the pin's reach (the pin is in the S of sec 22, BLM PLSS). Stocking's 'south side of the creek' 1/2-3/4 mi above the lake falls on the Norton and Cooper land (Jas. Norton 160 in NW sec 27; Jno. Norton 80 and H. Cooper 20 in S sec 22 E of the creek); no Stocking tract.
1894 and 1907 Kent plats: no Stocking land at the creek; a Parmus Stocking lived in Oakfield Twp in 1900 (census).
1880 census: Parmus T. Stocking in Grattan Twp (Oakfield by 1900); Frank Stocking, b. 1860 at Otisco/Belding, is likely the F. G. Stocking of the 1914 letter.
